headline: A rough session across the board — PLS tanks 6.3% and GXAI drops 4.7% as US markets sold off last night and Australian unemployment hits a five-year high.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS took another hit today, closing down 6.3% at $2.97. Lithium sentiment remains deeply subdued — there's no meaningful recovery in lithium prices in sight, and the stock is now down nearly 56% on your total investment. The long-term lithium thesis is intact (EVs still need it), but the timing of any recovery is very uncertain.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI fell 4.7% today, dragged down by a rough night on the NASDAQ last session — tech and AI stocks took a broad hit, with the NASDAQ down 1.88%. This ETF tracks AI-focused companies, so it amplifies moves in that space. The fund is now down about 12.6% on your total investment.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 1.8% last night in what was a broad tech sell-off on Wall Street. Nothing company-specific drove it — the whole NASDAQ was under pressure. The long-term AI and cloud story at Microsoft remains very strong, and Bloomberg is reporting the AI opportunity is actually growing bigger, not smaller.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google fell 1.68% last night, slightly more than the broader market. No major bad news — just caught up in the general tech pullback. Interestingly, Google just publicly released its new Gemini 4 Argon AI model, which is seen as finally catching up to rivals like GPT-6. Earnings are due October 28, which could be a catalyst.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 1.06% today, reflecting some softness in emerging market sentiment. The Middle East shipping tensions and a slightly weaker AUD added some pressure. Still only marginally below your invested amount — nothing alarming here.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS fell 0.89% today, tracking the US market weakness from last night's S&P 500 drop. This is still comfortably in the green overall (+4.9% on your investment), and a single down day in a diversified US market ETF is just normal noise.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped 0.67% today — a modest dip for a diversified ETF that holds global shares, bonds, and property. With exposure across many asset classes, it's naturally cushioned compared to pure equity plays. Sitting slightly below your invested amount, but nothing to worry about.

movers.name: DHHF ETF
movers.note: DHHF edged down 0.55% today — essentially flat. This broadly diversified shares ETF is doing exactly what it's supposed to: smooth out the bumps. Virtually breakeven on your investment overall.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: The one green number in the portfolio last night — TTWO nudged up 0.45%, bucking the broader tech sell-off. There's plenty of positive buzz around GTA 6, with Bloomberg publishing a detailed behind-the-scenes piece and reports of a potential PC release in early 2027. Rockstar's team also confirmed future games will be built faster using GTA 6's engine and tools.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium pain continues — hold and be patient
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals dropped another 6.3% today to $2.97, and is now down nearly 56% on your original investment. There's no near-term catalyst to reverse this — lithium prices remain depressed globally. But the long-term case (EV adoption, battery demand) hasn't disappeared. This is the kind of holding where selling now locks in the loss. Sit tight unless your conviction in the long-term story has genuinely changed.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF down 4.7% — broad tech sell-off, not a structural problem
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell hard today following last night's NASDAQ drop of 1.88%. This ETF amplifies moves in AI-exposed tech stocks, so big swings are normal. The AI investment theme is very much alive — Google just released Gemini 4 Argon publicly, and the IMF flagged AI as a key global economic risk (and opportunity). Down 12.6% overall, but if you believe in the AI megatrend long-term, this is a hold.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings Oct 28 — watch closely
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reports earnings on October 28 (US time). Motley Fool is tipping the stock to soar on the result. The release of Gemini 4 Argon — which reviewers say finally puts Google competitive with GPT-6 and Claude — could be a positive talking point on the call. Down 1.68% last night but still up 11.8% on your total investment. Hold into earnings; a good result could provide a solid lift.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Down last night but the AI story keeps getting bigger
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 1.8% last night in a general tech sell-off. Bloomberg ran a piece today arguing the AI bubble will actually grow bigger — and Microsoft is central to that story through its OpenAI partnership and Azure cloud. Still up over 20% on your investment. No reason to do anything here — just regular volatility in a strong long-term holding.

watch_today.title: Australia unemployment hits 5-year high — RBA rate hike now unlikely
watch_today.detail: New data today showed Australia's unemployment rate jumped to 4.7%, with nearly 40,000 jobs lost. This is the highest jobless rate in five years and puts real pressure on the RBA to hold off on any further interest rate increases. Lower rates are generally good for growth stocks and property — worth watching how this plays out at the next RBA meeting.

watch_today.title: Middle East shipping tensions pushing oil and gold — watch the flow-on
watch_today.detail: Attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz hit a wartime high this week, with Iran reportedly escalating tactics ahead of the US midterm elections. Oil (WTI) slipped to $93.77 last night despite the tension, but gold surged 1.38% to $4,164/oz — a classic 'safe haven' move. If the Hormuz situation escalates further, oil could spike and hit inflation globally. Keep an eye on it.

world.summary: The dominant global stories today centre on the US midterm elections and growing interference concerns, escalating Middle East shipping attacks near the Strait of Hormuz, and a warning from the IMF about global debt and economic risks.

stories.title: US midterms underway amid election interference fears and Department of Justice pressure on California
stories.why_it_matters: The US midterm elections are now underway, and there's serious concern about political interference in the process. The Trump administration's Justice Department has pressured California officials to withhold ballots for voters flagged on federal rolls — a move critics are calling voter suppression. Reuters outlines nine ways the Trump administration could interfere with results. Canada says the US is even 'monitoring' it for signs of foreign election meddling. The outcome of these midterms will shape the balance of power in the US Congress, which directly affects everything from fiscal policy to trade — all of which flows through to global markets.

stories.title: Iran escalating Hormuz shipping attacks before US midterms — oil and global trade at risk
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow channel through which about 20% of the world's oil passes — have hit a wartime high, according to Radio Free Europe. US officials say Iran is deliberately stepping up these attacks in the lead-up to the American midterm elections, likely to apply pressure. Saudi Arabia is also fighting the Iran-backed Houthi movement in Yemen and facing significant strategic problems doing so, according to ABC News analysis. If the Hormuz strait becomes seriously disrupted, oil prices could spike sharply, pushing up petrol prices and inflation worldwide — including here in Australia.

stories.title: IMF warns wealthy nations to cut debt and flags AI market crash as a key global risk
stories.why_it_matters: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) — essentially the world's economic referee — is sounding the alarm on two fronts. First, it's urging wealthy countries like the US and UK to rein in their massive government debts, warning that high debt loads are creating pressure on the global economy. Second, it specifically flagged an AI market correction (a potential crash in AI-related stocks), war, and debt as the three biggest risks to global growth. For investors with AI-heavy holdings like GXAI, this is a timely reminder that the AI theme carries real volatility risk.

stories.title: Middle East conflict sparking instability across Horn of Africa
stories.why_it_matters: The ongoing Middle East conflict is now spilling over into the Horn of Africa, reigniting fighting in an already fragile region. The Houthi movement — backed by Iran and based in Yemen — has long ties to actors in East Africa, and the escalation is stirring instability. This matters because the Horn of Africa sits at the mouth of the Red Sea, another critical global shipping lane. Disruption there adds to supply chain risks already being created by the Hormuz attacks.

stories.title: Middle East conflict creating new shipping opportunities for Africa via Cape of Good Hope route
stories.why_it_matters: There's a silver lining to the Red Sea crisis: African ports along the Cape of Good Hope route are booming as shipping companies reroute cargo to avoid conflict zones. Countries like South Africa, Kenya, and others with major ports are seeing increased trade traffic. It's a reminder that geopolitical crises don't just destroy value — they also redirect it, sometimes in unexpected directions.

markets.summary: Last night was a rough one on Wall Street — the NASDAQ dropped 1.88% and the S&P 500 fell 1.11%, dragging down tech stocks across the board. The ASX held up much better today, slipping just 0.09%. Gold surged on safe-haven demand while oil eased slightly despite Middle East tensions. The Aussie dollar softened slightly against the US dollar.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Nearly flat today — the ASX largely shrugged off last night's US weakness, a sign of some resilience in local stocks.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: A broad sell-off last night on Wall Street — fell 86 points. Macro concerns around midterm uncertainty and Middle East tensions weighed on sentiment.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech stocks took the brunt of the sell-off last night, down 511 points. AI and growth stocks hit hardest — flows into GXAI, GOOG and MSFT all reflected this.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dipped despite Hormuz shipping tensions — a surprising move. Markets may be pricing in demand concerns over Middle East supply risk for now.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged nearly 1.4% last night — investors parking money in safe haven assets amid election uncertainty and Middle East instability.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped slightly. Today's weak jobs data (unemployment at 4.7%, a five-year high) may be weighing on it — markets see less chance of RBA rate hikes now.

politics.summary: A big day for the Australian economy — unemployment jumped to a five-year high of 4.7%, nearly 40,000 jobs were lost, and the RBA is now under serious pressure to stop raising interest rates. There's also political action on digital regulation and health insurance.

stories.title: Australia's unemployment rate hits 4.7% — a five-year high — after nearly 40,000 jobs lost
stories.why_it_matters: Australia lost close to 40,000 jobs last month, pushing the unemployment rate to 4.7% — the highest it's been in five years. The Conversation reports this makes a further RBA interest rate hike much less likely, as the central bank won't want to tip more people out of work. For everyday Aussies, this means mortgage holders may get some relief. For investors, it signals the economy is cooling, which could eventually push the RBA toward cutting rates — generally a positive for shares and property values.

stories.title: Greens block Labor's bill to cut private health insurance rebate
stories.why_it_matters: Labor wanted to reduce the government rebate that subsidises private health insurance premiums, as part of a broader budget savings measure. The Greens blocked it in the Senate, arguing the changes didn't adequately protect pensioners. The bill has now stalled. If you hold private health insurance or have parents who do, this means no immediate change to the rebate — but the issue hasn't gone away and may come back to parliament.

stories.title: Labor's Digital Duty of Care bill draws fierce criticism as 'state censorship'
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is pushing a 'Digital Duty of Care' bill that would impose legal obligations on social media platforms to protect users from harm online. Critics, including US commentator Michael Shellenberger and The Australian newspaper, are calling it 'radical state censorship' and 'absurd.' Supporters say platforms like Facebook and TikTok need to be held accountable for the content they amplify. This is shaping up as a major political fight — and has implications for how Australians use social media and what tech companies can operate here.

stories.title: Coalition moves to block Albanese government selling Victoria Barracks in Sydney
stories.why_it_matters: The opposition Coalition has introduced a bill in parliament to prevent the Labor government from selling Victoria Barracks in inner Sydney. The historic military site has been eyed as a potential source of revenue or housing redevelopment. The Coalition argues it should remain in public hands. This adds to broader debate about what to do with Defence-owned land in expensive urban areas.

ai.summary: Google has publicly released its Gemini 4 Argon AI model, finally catching up to rivals OpenAI and Anthropic in the top tier of AI competition. Regulators around the world are debating how to govern AI across different sectors.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon publicly — finally competitive with GPT-6 and Claude
stories.why_it_matters: Google has publicly launched Gemini 4 Argon, its most advanced AI model yet. Reviewers say it delivers performance 'comparable to Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra' — meaning Google has finally caught up in what has been a bruising race with OpenAI (ChatGPT) and Anthropic (Claude). In practical terms, Gemini 4 Argon can do what the best AI tools can do: reason through complex problems, write code, analyse documents and images. For GOOG investors, this is significant — Google's AI credibility directly affects advertiser confidence and cloud business growth. The Argon model is priced at roughly half of Claude Opus 5.5 according to one comparison.

stories.title: UK government releases AI strategy for healthcare — 10 key takeaways
stories.why_it_matters: The UK government has released a formal AI strategy specifically for the healthcare sector, setting out how hospitals, doctors, and regulators should use and oversee AI tools in clinical settings. It's one of the most detailed government AI plans released by any major nation in a specific industry sector. The UK approach — which tries to balance innovation with patient safety — is likely to influence how Australia and other countries think about regulating medical AI.

stories.title: UK's financial regulator (FCA) plans to use AI to automate its own regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) — the body that regulates banks and financial firms — has announced plans to use AI to automate parts of its own regulatory work. In plain English: the financial cop is going to use AI to watch the financial industry. This could mean faster identification of rule-breaking, more consistent enforcement, and cheaper compliance costs for firms. It's a sign that AI is moving well beyond tech companies and into the heart of government.

stories.title: The AI race is back on — and it's heating up fast
stories.why_it_matters: The Verge published a big-picture piece today arguing the AI race between Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and others is back in full swing after a period of consolidation. With Google's Gemini 4 Argon launch and ongoing model updates from competitors, the pace of AI development is accelerating again. For investors in GXAI (AI ETF) or GOOG and MSFT individually, this competitive intensity is a double-edged sword — it drives innovation but also drives massive spending on data centres and chips, which eats into near-term profits.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done — Roosters beat the Knights 19-18 in a thriller. Now it's all about player movement, Kangaroos squad announcements ahead of the Rugby League World Cup, and a wild AFL trade period wrapping up.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights in a classic
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters defeated the Newcastle Knights 19-18 at Accor Stadium on Sunday October 4, in what was a nail-biter of a Grand Final. One point in it at the death — it doesn't get much tighter than that. The Roosters clinched their latest premiership with an incredibly narrow margin. Knights fans will be heartbroken.

stories.title: Kangaroos squad named: Kevvie makes surprise calls, Bostock gets debut, Samoa pulls off World Cup stunner
stories.why_it_matters: Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters ('Kevvie') has named his squad for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup, with some eyebrow-raising selections and omissions. Queensland centre Selwyn Bostock earns his debut call-up after a remarkable rise from adversity — Fox Sports has a detailed piece on the setbacks that shaped him. Meanwhile, Samoa pulled off a stunning result to qualify for the World Cup, shaking up the international landscape heading into the tournament.

stories.title: Bears head coach role emerges — potential blow to Knights after Grand Final heartbreak
stories.why_it_matters: Just days after their Grand Final heartbreak, Newcastle Knights are facing more potential turbulence — a coaching candidate has emerged for the North Sydney Bears head coach role that could lure staff or personnel away from the club. Fox Sports reports this is a 'potential blow' for the high-flying Knights as they try to rebuild for next season after coming so agonisingly close to a title.

stories.title: AFL trade period wraps up — Richmond snags extra top-5 pick, Adelaide reject huge Murray offer, Dees eye pick swap
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade period is in full swing with some big moves. Richmond has secured an additional top-5 draft pick, boosting their rebuild significantly. Adelaide rejected what 7NEWS describes as a 'huge offer' from North Melbourne for defender Nick Murray — the AFL world is in disbelief at the knockback. Melbourne are eyeing a pick swap to strengthen their draft hand. Fox Sports has a mega wrap of what all 18 clubs did in the trade period, with draft hands now taking shape before the national draft.
